**Naming of the Surah**

• It is called Al-A'raf (The Heights), because it uniquely recounts the account of the people of al-A'raf on the Day of Resurrection. They are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so they deserve neither Paradise for their good deeds nor the Fire for their bad deeds. Al-A'raf is the highest part of the wall that separates Paradise from the Fire, as its mention in Surat al-Hadid [verse 13] is in the wording (سور) (sur, "wall").

**From the Objectives of the Surah**

• The surah presents situations of calling to faith and warning, and the consequences of turning away from the call of God, in many forms. At times the context takes the form of the story of Iblis with Adam; at other times, the stories of the Prophets with their peoples, each story ending with punishment for whoever opposed the command of God. At other times the context takes the form of a scene from the scenes of the Resurrection, in which the fates of the deniers are revealed, along with the fates of those who obeyed the Lord of the worlds.

• The prohibition of taking partners besides God, and the warning to the polytheists of the evil consequence of associating partners with God in this world and the Hereafter, and the description of the severe punishment that befell the polytheists in this world and what will befall them in the Hereafter.

• Reminding people of the blessing of the creation of the earth and their being empowered with its good things, and reminding them of God's blessing upon the human species through the creation of their origin and their honoring; and reminding them of the enmity of Satan, deeply rooted toward humankind, through his refusal to prostrate to their father Adam and his scheming against him, and the continuation of that enmity until the Hour; and warning people against falling into the deception of Satan, through his enticing them to deprive themselves of good things and to commit what will cause them punishment in the Hereafter.

• The description of the terrors that will befall the criminals on the Day of Recompense, and the honors that will be granted to the God-conscious (al-muttaqun); the reminder of resurrection and the explanation of its proofs; and mention of a scene from the scenes of the Day of Resurrection in the form of the dialogue between the people of Paradise, the people of the Fire, and the companions of al-A'raf.

• An extensive account of the stories of the Messengers with their peoples, and what they encountered of their obstinacy and harm; and warning people not to be deceived by God's granting respite to His servants before the descent of punishment, as a way of giving them an excuse, for punishment comes suddenly without prior warning.

• Rebuke of the polytheists for their contentment with polytheism instead of al-hanifiyyah (the upright, pure monotheistic faith), and the striking of an example with one whom God gave His signs, but Satan whispered to him, so he abandoned guidance; and the description of the state of the people of misguidance in their worship of what neither hears, nor sees, nor benefits, nor harms, and the description of their deities with what contradicts divinity.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 86:

Do not sit on every road threatening people with killing if they do not give you their wealth, and blocking those who believe in God from the straight path of God, those who believe in Him, the Mighty and Majestic, and do righteous deeds. You seek to make the way of God crooked, bending it to follow your desires and turning people away from following it. Remember God's favor upon you when your number was small and He multiplied you, so that you became strong and honored. Look at how the end of those who spread corruption on earth was, and what destruction and ruin befell them?

This is a passage from the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 87. The verse itself reads:

﴿And if there is a group of you who have believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who have not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us. And He is the best of judges.﴾

The commentary explains: If there is a group among you who believed in what Allah sent me with, and a group who did not believe in it, then wait, you deniers, for the decree of Allah that will separate between us and you, when His punishment that I warned you of descends upon you. And Allah, exalted is He, is the best of judges among His servants.

The leaders and the elite among the people of Shu'ayb, who were too proud to believe in Allah and follow His messenger Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), said: "We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you, from our land, unless you return to our religion." Shu'ayb said, denouncing and marveling at their words: "Would we follow you in your religion and your false creed, even though we are averse to it, having known its falsehood?"

Shu'ayb said to his people, correcting himself: "We would be inventing a lie against God if we returned to your religion after God has rescued us from it. It is not for us to revert to anything other than the religion of our Lord, unless our Lord wills it. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge, and He knows what is good for His servants. In God alone do we place our trust, for guidance and for victory. Our Lord, judge between us and our people with truth, for You are the best of judges."

The chiefs and the arrogant leaders, who denied and rejected the call to monotheism, said, persisting in their insolence and rebellion and warning against following Shu'ayb: "If you follow Shu'ayb, then you will surely be ruined."
So the severe earthquake seized the people of Shu'ayb, and by morning they lay dead in their homes, fallen face down.

Those who denied Shu'ayb were as though they had never dwelt in their homes or enjoyed them, for they were utterly uprooted, and no trace of them remained. Loss and destruction befell them in this world and in the Hereafter.

Then Shu'ayb turned away from them when he became certain that the punishment had come down upon them, and said: "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord, and I advised you to enter the religion of God and to give up what you were upon, but you did not listen and did not obey. So how could I grieve over a people who denied the oneness of God and rejected His messengers?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 94:

We did not send a prophet to any town without afflicting its people with hardship and adversity, so that they might humble themselves. He would call them to worship God and forbid them from the polytheism (shirk) they were engaged in, but his people would deny him. We afflicted them with adversity and hardship: we struck their bodies with sicknesses and diseases, and their wealth with poverty and need, hoping that they would humble themselves, turn back in repentance to God, and return to the truth.

Then We replaced the bad condition with a good one, the first state of ease. So they became healthy in their bodies and enjoyed abundance and prosperity in their wealth, as a respite for them, and so that they might give thanks. But all of that did not benefit them, and they did not take heed or desist from what they were engaged in. They said, "This is the custom of time with its people: a day of good and a day of ill, and this is what happened to our forefathers before us." So We seized them with punishment suddenly while they were secure, the thought of destruction never occurring to them.

If the people of the towns had believed their messengers, followed them, and avoided what Allah had forbidden them, He would have opened to them the doors of goodness from every direction. But they denied, so Allah seized them with a destroying punishment because of their disbelief and their sins.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "The Simplified Exegesis") on Surah 7, verse 97:**

Do the people of the towns think that they are safe and secure from the punishment of God, that it will not come upon them by night while they are asleep?

Do the people of the towns feel secure that the punishment of God will not come upon them in the forenoon while they are heedless, busied with the affairs of their worldly life? God specified these two times for mention because a person is most heedless during them, so the coming of punishment at these times is more dreadful and more severe.

Do the people of the towns that denied the truth feel safe from Allah's plan and from His granting them respite? He grants them respite as a gradual lure, through the blessings He bestowed on them in this world, as a punishment for their scheming. None feel safe from Allah's plan except the people who are destined for ruin.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 100:

Has it not become clear to those who inherited the land after its former people were destroyed for their sins, that if We willed, We could afflict them with punishment for their sins, as We did to their predecessors? And We seal their hearts, so that truth does not enter them, and they do not hear admonition or reminder?

These are the cities whose mention has preceded: they are the cities of the peoples of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb. We relate to you, O Messenger, some of their news, and of the matter of the messengers of God who were sent to them, which contains a lesson for those who take heed and a warning for the wrongdoers. Our messengers came to the people of these cities with clear proofs of their truthfulness, yet they were not going to believe in what the messengers brought them, because of their insolence and their denial of the truth. Just as God sealed the hearts of these disbelievers who were mentioned, God seals the hearts of the disbelievers in Muhammad (ﷺ).

We did not find in most of the earlier nations any trustworthiness or fulfilment of covenant. We found most of them to be transgressors, departing from the obedience of Allah and compliance with His command.

Then after those messengers mentioned earlier, We sent Musa (Moses) son of Imran with Our clear signs to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his people, but they denied them and disbelieved in them out of wrongdoing and obstinacy. So look, O Messenger, with insight, at how We dealt with them, and how We drowned them all to the last one in the sight of Musa and his people. Such is the end of those who spread corruption.
Moses said to Pharaoh, in dialogue and as one delivering the message: "Indeed, I am a messenger from Allah, the Creator of all creatures and the Manager of their affairs and their final outcomes."

It is fitting that I say nothing about God except the truth, and it is right for me to hold to it. I have come to you with a proof and a clear evidence from your Lord confirming the truth of what I tell you. So release the Children of Israel with me, O Pharaoh, from your bondage and oppression, and let them go to worship God.

Pharaoh said to Moses: "If you have come with a sign, as you claim, then produce it and bring it before me, so that your claim may be confirmed and your truthfulness established, if you are truthful in what you have asserted, that you are a messenger of the Lord of the worlds."
Then Moses threw down his staff, and it turned into a great serpent, plainly visible to the eyes.

And he drew his hand out from the opening of his collar, which was open at the chest, or from under his armpit, and behold, it was white like milk, without any leprosy, a sign for Pharaoh. Then, when he returned it, it went back to its original colour, like the rest of his body.

The nobles of Pharaoh's people said: "Indeed, this Moses is a sorcerer who bewitches the eyes of the people through his deception of them, until he makes them imagine that the staff is a serpent, while the thing is other than what it really is. He is well-versed in sorcery and skilled in it."
He wants to drive all of you out of your land. Pharaoh said: "What do you advise me to do, O nobles, concerning the matter of Moses?"

Those among Pharaoh's people who attended the debate with Moses, the chiefs and nobles of Pharaoh's people, said: "Put off Moses and his brother Aaron, and send heralds to the cities and provinces of «Egypt» to gather the police."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 112:

That they may bring you every skilled sorcerer.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 7, Verse 113:**

﴿And the magicians came to Pharaoh, saying, "Will we indeed have a reward and wealth if we overcome Moses?"﴾
Pharaoh said: "Yes, you will have the reward, and you will be close to me if you overcome him."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 115:

Pharaoh's magicians said to Musa, with arrogance and disregard: "O Musa, you choose whether you throw your staff first, or we throw first."

Moses said to the magicians: "You throw first." So when they threw down their ropes and staffs, they bewitched the eyes of the people, made them imagine what they had done was real, when it was nothing but mere trickery and illusion, and they terrified the people with great terror. And they brought a powerful and great magic.

And Allah revealed to His servant and messenger Musa (peace be upon him) at that momentous occasion, in which Allah distinguished between truth and falsehood, commanding him to throw down what is in his right hand, which was his staff. So he threw it, and behold, it swallowed up what they had fabricated, and they had deceived the people into thinking it was true when it was false.

The truth was made manifest and became clear to those who witnessed it and were present for the matter of Musa (peace be upon him), and that he was a messenger of Allah calling to the truth; and the falsehood that they had been practising was nullified.
So all the magicians were overcome at the place where they had gathered, and Pharaoh and his people went away humbled, subdued, and defeated.
The magicians fell down prostrating on their faces to Allah, Lord of the worlds, because of what they had witnessed of the great power of Allah.
﴿They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds."﴾
He is the Lord of Musa and Harun, and He alone is the one to whom worship must be directed, to the exclusion of anyone else.

Pharaoh said to the magicians: "Have you believed in Allah before I gave you permission to do so? Indeed, this belief of yours in Allah, your affirmation of Moses, and your acknowledgment of his prophethood is a scheme that you and Moses have devised, so that you might expel the people of your city from it and be the ones who monopolize its good things. But you will soon know, O magicians, what punishment and torment will befall you."

Pharaoh said, as an explicit threat to the sorcerers: "I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, O sorcerers: the right hand with the left foot, or the left hand with the right foot. Then I will surely crucify you all upon the trunks of palm trees, as an exemplary punishment for you and to terrify the people."

The sorcerers said to Pharaoh: "We are certain that to our Lord we shall return, and that His punishment is more severe than your punishment. So we shall endure today your punishment, so that we may be saved from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 126:

You, O Pharaoh, find fault with us and disapprove of us only because we believed and affirmed the proofs of our Lord and His signs which Moses brought. You and no one else can produce the like of them, except Allah, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Our Lord, pour upon us great patience and steadfastness in it, and cause us to die as those who submit to Your command and follow Your Messenger.

The chiefs and nobles of Pharaoh's people said to Pharaoh: "Will you leave Moses and his people, the Children of Israel, to cause corruption in the land [of Egypt] by changing their religion, worshipping God alone without any partner, and abandoning your worship and the worship of your gods?" Pharaoh said: "We will kill the sons of the Children of Israel and spare their women alive for service, and indeed we are dominant over them with the power of sovereignty and authority."

Moses said to his people, the Children of Israel: "Seek help from Allah against Pharaoh and his people, and be patient with what has befallen you from Pharaoh of hardships, both in yourselves and in your children. Indeed, the earth entirely belongs to Allah; He bequeaths it to whomever of His servants He wills, and the praiseworthy outcome is for those who fear Allah, obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions."

The Children of Israel said to their prophet Musa: "We were tormented and harmed, with our sons being slaughtered and our women being spared, at the hands of Fir'awn and his people, both before you came to us and after you came to us." Musa said to them: "Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy Fir'awn and his people, and will make you successors in their land after their destruction, so that He may see how you act: will you be thankful or ungrateful?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 130:

And We certainly afflicted the people of Pharaoh with drought and famine, and with a decrease in their fruits and crops, so that they might take heed, refrain from their misguidance, and turn humbly to their Lord in repentance.

When prosperity and provision came to Pharaoh and his people, they said, "This is ours, by our deserving it." And if misfortune—drought and famine—befell them, they would take it as an omen of ill and say, "This is because of Moses and those with him." Truly, what befalls them of drought and famine is only by the decree and predestination of Allah, and because of their sins and their disbelief. But most of the people of Pharaoh do not know this, because they are immersed in ignorance and error.

The commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 132:

"And the people of Pharaoh said to Musa: Whatever sign you bring us, and whatever proof and evidence you establish, to turn us away from what we are upon of the religion of Pharaoh, we will not believe you."

Then We sent upon them a overwhelming flood that drowned their crops and fruits. And We sent the locusts, which devoured their crops, their fruits, their doors, their roofs, and their clothing. And We sent the lice (al-qummal), which spoiled the fruits and destroyed both animals and plants. And We sent the frogs, which filled their vessels, their food, and their beds. And We also sent blood, so that their rivers and wells turned into blood, and they could find no water fit for drinking. These are signs from the signs of God, which none but Him can bring about, each separate from the others. Yet despite all this, the people of Pharaoh grew arrogant, becoming too proud to believe in God, and they were a people who practiced what God had forbidden of sins and transgression, in insolence and rebellion.

When the punishment fell upon Pharaoh and his people, they turned in fear to Moses and said: "O Moses, pray to your Lord for us, by the covenant He has revealed to you, to lift the punishment from us through repentance. If you lift from us the punishment we are in, we will surely believe in what you have brought, we will surely follow what you have called us to, and we will surely let the Children of Israel go with you, and we will not prevent them from going wherever they wish."

When God lifted from them the punishment He had sent upon them, until a term they were bound to reach without fail, so that they would be punished at it, what had preceded for them of reprieve and the removal of the punishment did not benefit them until it befell them. Behold, they broke the covenants they had made with their Lord and with Moses, and persisted in their disbelief and misguidance.

So We took vengeance on them when the appointed time for their destruction arrived, by sending down Our retribution upon them, which was their drowning in the sea, because they denied the signs that appeared at the hands of Musa, and they were heedless of these signs; and that heedlessness was the cause of their denial.

And We caused the Children of Israel, who had been oppressed and made to serve, to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land (namely the land of al-Sham, "the Levant"), which We had blessed, by bringing forth crops, fruits and rivers. And the good word of your Lord, O Messenger, was fulfilled for the Children of Israel through the establishment of their authority in the land, because of their patience in bearing the harm of Pharaoh and his people. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been building, such as their structures and gardens, and what they had been constructing of buildings, palaces and other things.

And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea. Then they came upon a people devoted to and persistent in worshipping their idols. The Children of Israel said: "O Musa, make for us a god (ṣanam) to worship, just as these people have their idols that they worship." Musa said to them: "Indeed you are a people who are ignorant of the greatness of Allah, and you do not know that worship is not befitting except for Allah, the One, the Subduer."

Indeed, these people who persist in worshipping these idols—their polytheism is doomed to destruction, and what they have been doing by worshipping those idols is destroyed and void, for those idols cannot ward off God's punishment when it befalls them.

Moses said to his people: "Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, while it is Allah who created you and preferred you over the worlds of your time, through the abundance of prophets among you and the destruction of your enemy, and what He singled you out with of the signs?"

Remember, O Children of Israel, Our blessings upon you when We rescued you from the captivity of Pharaoh and his people, and from the humiliation and degradation you suffered: the slaughter of your sons and the sparing of your women for service and humiliation, and being subjected to the most vile and cruel torment. Then Our deliverance of you was a trial from Allah for you and a great blessing.

God Almighty appointed Moses a meeting to commune with his Lord for thirty nights. Then He added ten more nights to the term, so the appointed time set by God for Moses to speak with Him was completed as forty nights. Moses said to his brother Aaron, when he intended to set out to commune with his Lord: "Be my successor among my people until I return, and lead them to obedience to God and to worshipping Him, and do not follow the way of those who spread corruption in the earth."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 143:

When Musa came at the appointed time, which was the completion of forty nights, and his Lord spoke to him with what He spoke of His revelation, His command and His prohibition, he hoped to see Allah, so he asked to look upon Him. Allah said to him: ﴿You will not see Me﴾, meaning: you will not be able to see Me in this world. ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place when I manifest Myself to it, then you will see Me﴾. So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, levelled with the ground, and Musa fell down unconscious. When he recovered from his swoon he said: "Glory be to You, O Lord, exalted above what is unfitting to Your majesty. I have turned to You in repentance from my request to You to see You in this worldly life, and I am the first of the believers in You among my people."

God said: "O Musa, I have chosen you above the people by My messages to My creation, to whom I have sent you, and by My speaking to you without an intermediary. So take what I have given you of My commands and prohibitions, hold fast to it, act upon it, and be among those who give thanks to God, the Exalted, for what He has granted you of His message and for having singled you out with His speech."

We wrote for Musa on the Tablets, from every matter he needs in his religion of rulings, as an admonition to restrain and a lesson, and a detailed explanation of the obligations of the lawful and the unlawful, the commands and prohibitions, the stories, the beliefs, the reports, and the unseen matters. Allah said to him: ﴿Take hold of it with strength﴾, i.e., take the Torah earnestly and with diligence, and command your people to act upon what Allah has legislated in it. For whoever among them and among others associates partners with Him, I will show him in the Hereafter the abode of the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqin), which is the Fire of Allah that He prepared for His enemies who go out of obedience to Him.

I will turn away from understanding the proofs and evidences that point to My greatness, My law, and My rulings the hearts of those who are arrogant toward obeying Me, and who are arrogant toward people without right. So they do not follow a prophet nor listen to him, because of their arrogance. And if these people who are too proud to believe see every sign, they will not believe in it, due to their turning away and their opposition to God and His Messenger. And if they see the path of righteousness, they will not take it as a path; and if they see the path of error, that is disbelief, they will take it as a path and a religion. That is because of their denial of the signs of God and their heedlessness of reflecting upon them and contemplating their indications.

Those who denied Allah's signs and proofs, and the meeting with Allah in the Hereafter, their deeds have become void, because the condition for their acceptance was absent, namely faith in Allah and belief in His recompense. They will not be recompensed in the Hereafter except with the recompense of what they used to do in this world of disbelief and sins, which is abiding forever in the Fire.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 148:

And the people of Musa, after he had departed from them to proceed to his Lord's appointed meeting, took for worship a calf made of their gold, a body without a soul, which had a sound resembling the lowing of a cow. Did they not see that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to any good? They went ahead with this monstrous matter that they undertook, and they were wrongdoers to themselves, placing things in other than their proper place.

When those who had worshipped the calf regretted it, after Musa returned to them, and they saw that they had gone astray from the right path and had turned away from the religion of Allah, they began to acknowledge their servitude and seek forgiveness, saying: "If our Lord does not have mercy on us by accepting our repentance and covering our sins with it, we will surely be among the lost, whose deeds have gone to waste."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 150:

When Musa (Moses) returned to his people from the Children of Israel, angry and grieved, because Allah had informed him that He had tested his people and that al-Samiri had led them astray, Musa said: "Evil is the successorship you have carried out after me. Did you hasten the command of your Lord?" That is: did you hasten my coming to you, when it was decreed by Allah, the Exalted? Musa threw down the tablets of the Torah in anger at his people who worshipped the calf, and in anger at his brother Harun (Aaron). He seized his brother by the head, dragging him towards himself. Harun said, seeking to placate him: "O son of my mother! Indeed the people made me weak, considered me feeble, and nearly killed me. So do not let the enemies rejoice at what you do to me, and do not place me in your anger with the people who disobeyed your command and worshipped the calf."

Musa said, once his brother's excuse had become clear to him and he knew that Harun had not fallen short in what he was commanded by Allah: "My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your wide mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 152:

Indeed, those who took the calf (as a god) will be overtaken by severe wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world, because of their disbelief in their Lord. And just as We did to those (people), We shall do to the fabricators (al-muftarin) and the innovators (al-mubtadi'in) in the religion of Allah. Every possessor of an innovation (bid'ah) is humbled.

And those who committed evil deeds, [such as] disbelief and sins, and then repented after doing them and returned to faith and righteous deeds — indeed your Lord, after sincere repentance, is All-Forgiving of their deeds, not exposing them by them, and Most Merciful toward them and toward everyone like them among those who repent.
When Musa's anger had subsided, he picked up the Tablets, after he had thrown them down, and in them was guidance and mercy for those who fear Allah and dread His punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 155:

And Musa chose seventy men from his people, the best of them, and set out with them to Mount Sinai (Tur Sina'), at the appointed time that Allah had promised to meet him there with them, for repentance from what the foolish ones among the Children of Israel had done in worshipping the calf. When they reached that place, they said: "We will not believe you, O Musa, until we see Allah plainly (jahratan). For you have spoken with Him, so show Him to us." Then the violent earthquake seized them, and they died. Musa stood up, supplicating to Allah and saying: "My Lord, what shall I say to the Children of Israel when I come to them, after You have destroyed their best? If You had willed, You could have destroyed them all, and me with them, before this situation. That would have been easier for me. Will You destroy us for what the foolish ones among us have done? This act that my people committed, worshipping the calf, is nothing but a trial and a test, by which You lead astray whom You will of Your creation and guide whom You will. You are our Protector and our Helper, so forgive our sins, have mercy upon us with Your mercy, and You are the best of those who pardon wrongdoing and overlook sins."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 156:

"And ordain for us good in this world and in the Hereafter, for we have turned back to You in repentance." He said: "My punishment I inflict upon whom I will of My creation, and My mercy encompasses all things. So I will ordain it for those who fear Allah and dread His punishment, who perform His obligations and avoid His prohibitions, and those who affirm the proofs and evidences of His oneness."

This mercy I will prescribe for those who fear Allah and avoid His disobedience, and who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, who neither reads nor writes, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ), whose description and command they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. He commands them to monotheism (tawhid) and obedience, and to everything whose goodness is known, and forbids them from polytheism (shirk) and disobedience, and everything whose ugliness is known. He makes lawful for them the good things of food, drink and marriage, and makes unlawful for them the foul things among them, such as the flesh of swine, and what they used to consider lawful of foods and drinks which Allah had forbidden. He also removes from them the burdensome obligations imposed upon them, such as cutting off the place of impurity from a garment, burning the spoils of war, and retaliation (qisas), which is definitely required from one who kills intentionally, whether the killing was intentional or by error. So those who believed in the unlettered Prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ), acknowledged his prophethood, honored, exalted and supported him, followed the Qur'an revealed to him, and acted upon his Sunnah (the Prophet's way), those are the successful ones, [attaining] what Allah has promised His believing servants.

Say, [O Messenger], to all of mankind: "Indeed, I am the Messenger of God to you all, not to some of you without others, the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. Divinity and worship are not fitting for anyone except Him, exalted is His praise, the One Who is capable of creating creation, annihilating it, and resurrecting it. So believe in God and affirm His oneness, and believe in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), the unlettered Prophet, who believes in God and in what was revealed to him from his Lord and what was revealed to the prophets before him. Follow this Messenger and commit yourselves to acting upon what he has commanded you of obedience to God, in the hope that you will be guided to the straight path."
Among the people of Moses, the Children of Israel, there is a community that stands upright upon the truth. They guide people by it, and they act justly by it in judging their disputes.

We divided the people of Musa (Moses) from the Children of Israel into twelve tribes, according to the number of the tribes (asbat), who were the sons of Ya'qub (Jacob), each tribe known by its leader (naqib). And We revealed to Musa, when his people asked him for water as they became thirsty in the wilderness (al-tih): "Strike the stone with your staff." So he struck it, and there gushed forth from it twelve springs of water. Each of the twelve tribes knew its drinking place, and no tribe would intrude upon another in its drinking. We shaded them with clouds, and We sent down upon them manna, which is a substance resembling gum, whose taste is like honey, and quails (al-salwa), which is a bird resembling the quail (al-sumana). We said to them: ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you﴾. But they disliked that and grew weary of it because of the long persistence in it, and they said: ﴿We will not endure one kind of food﴾, and they asked to exchange what is inferior for what is better. And they did not wrong Us when they did not give thanks to Allah and did not fulfill what Allah had made obligatory upon them; rather, they were wronging themselves, for they forfeited for themselves every good and exposed themselves to evil and retribution.

And mention, O Messenger, the disobedience of the Children of Israel toward their Lord, glorified and exalted is He, and toward their prophet Musa (peace be upon him), and their substitution of the words they were commanded to say when Allah said to them: "Dwell in this town, [Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)], and eat from its fruits, grains and plants wherever and whenever you wish, and say: 'Remove from us our sins,' and enter the gate prostrating humbly to Allah; We will forgive you your misdeeds, and We will not hold you accountable for them, and We will increase the reward of the good-doers from the good of both this world and the Hereafter."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 162:

So those among them who disbelieved in Allah changed the word that Allah had commanded them to say, and they entered the gate dragging themselves on their backsides, and they said, "A grain in a hair." So We sent down upon them a punishment from the sky, by which We destroyed them, because of their wrongdoing and their disobedience.

Ask them, O Messenger, about the story of the town that was by the sea, when its people transgressed on the Sabbath concerning the sacred ordinances of God. He had commanded them to honor the Sabbath day and not to hunt fish on it. God tested them and put them to trial. Their fish would come to them on the Sabbath in great numbers, visible on the surface of the water close to the shore; but when the Sabbath day passed, the fish would go off into the sea, and they would see none of them. So they would devise ways to trap the fish on the Sabbath in pits and catch them after it. Just as we have described to you this test and trial, by making the fish appear on the surface of the water on the day when it was forbidden for them to hunt them, and hiding them from them on the day when hunting them was permitted, so too do We test them because of their wickedness, their deviation from obedience to God and their departure from it.

And remember, O Messenger, when a group among them said to another group that was admonishing the transgressors on the Sabbath day and forbidding them from disobeying Allah therein: "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy in this world for their disobedience to Him, or whom He will punish with a severe punishment in the Hereafter?" Those who were forbidding them from disobeying Allah said: "We admonish them and forbid them so that we may be free of blame before Allah concerning them, and so that we may fulfill the duty Allah has placed upon us of enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil, and in hope that they may become mindful of Allah, fear Him, and repent of their disobedience to their Lord and their transgression against what He has forbidden them."

Then, when the group that had transgressed on the Sabbath abandoned what they had been reminded of, persisted in their deviance and their transgression therein, and did not heed what the admonishing group had advised them, God delivered those who forbade evil from His disobedience, and seized those who had transgressed on the Sabbath with a painful, severe punishment, because of their defiance of God's command and their departure from His obedience.

When that group persisted in its rebellion and transgressed what Allah had forbidden them, namely hunting on the Sabbath, Allah said to them: "Be apes, despised and expelled, distanced from every good." And so they became.

And remember, O Messenger, when your Lord declared clearly that He would surely send against the Jews those who would make them suffer the worst torment and humiliation until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, your Lord, O Messenger, is swift in punishment for whoever deserves it because of his disbelief and disobedience, and indeed He is Most Forgiving toward the sins of those who repent, and Most Merciful to them.

We dispersed the Children of Israel throughout the earth in groups. Among them were those who upheld the rights of God and the rights of His servants, and among them were those who fell short and wronged themselves. We tested these people with ease and comfort in living and abundance in provision, and We also tested them with hardship in living, calamities and misfortunes, in the hope that they would return to obedience to their Lord and repent of His disobedience.

Then there came after those whom We have described a bad succession: they inherited the Book from their predecessors, read it and knew it, yet they violated its rulings. They take whatever worldly goods come their way, from base gains such as bribery and other things, owing to their intense greed and avarice. Yet they say, along with that: "God will forgive us our sins," expecting from God falsehoods, and if the goods of this [lowly world] come to these Jews, they take them and deem them lawful, persisting in their sins and in their taking of what is forbidden. Was not a covenant taken from them to establish the Torah and act by what is in it, and not to say about God except the truth, and not to lie against Him? They knew what is in the Book yet they neglected it, abandoned acting by it, and violated the covenant of God made with them concerning that. "And the Last Abode is better for those who fear God," that is, those who obey His commands and avoid His prohibitions. Will you not then reason, you who take base gains, that what is with God is better and more lasting for the God-fearing?

﴿And those who hold fast to the Book, and establish the prayer — indeed, We shall not allow to be lost the reward of the righteous.﴾

Hmm, I should translate the passage itself, not the verse. Here is the translation of the commentary:

Those who hold fast to the Book, acting upon what it contains of beliefs and rulings, and who maintain the prayer within its prescribed limits, not neglecting its appointed times — indeed, Allah will reward them for their good deeds, and He will not let them go to waste.

Remember, O Messenger, when We lifted the mountain above the Children of Israel as though it were a cloud overshadowing them, and they became certain that it would fall upon them if they did not accept the rulings of the Torah. And We said to them: "Take what We have given you with determination," that is, act upon what We have bestowed upon you with diligence on your part, and remember what is in Our Book of covenants and pledges which We took from you to act upon what is in it, so that you may be mindful of your Lord and thereby be saved from His punishment.

Remember, O Messenger, when your Lord brought forth from the loins of the children of Adam their offspring, and made them testify concerning His Oneness, through what He placed in their natural disposition (fitrah) of the fact that He is their Lord, their Creator, and their Sovereign. So they acknowledged this, lest they deny it on the Day of Resurrection, and say that they did not admit it, or that the proof of God was not established against them, and that they had no knowledge of it, but were heedless of it.

Or lest you say: "Only our forefathers associated others with God before us, and they broke the covenant, so we followed them after them. Will You then punish us for what those who nullified their deeds did, by making a partner with God in worship?"

And just as We have explained the signs in detail, and made clear within them what We did to the earlier nations, so too do We explain the signs in detail and make them clear to your people, O Messenger, in the hope that they will turn away from their polytheism and turn back in repentance to their Lord.

Recount to your community, O Messenger, the story of the man from the Children of Israel to whom We gave Our signs and proofs, so he learned them, then disbelieved in them and cast them behind his back. Then Satan overpowered him, and he became one of the misguided who perish, because he disobeyed his Lord's command and obeyed Satan.

If We had willed, We would have raised him up through the signs We gave him, and enabled him to act upon them. But he clung to the earth and followed his own desire, preferring his pleasures and appetites over the Hereafter, and he refused to obey Allah and opposed His command. The likeness of such a man is the likeness of a dog: if you chase it away or leave it alone, it lolls out its tongue, panting in either case. Likewise, the one who has stripped himself of the signs of Allah remains in his disbelief, whether you strive hard in calling him or neglect him. This description, O Messenger, is the description of those people who were astray before you brought them guidance and the message. So relate to them, O Messenger, the accounts of the past nations, for in your telling of them lies the greatest of miracles; perhaps your people will reflect upon what you have brought them and believe in you.
Evil is the example of the people who denied the proofs and signs of Allah, rejected them, and wronged themselves by their denial of these proofs and signs.

Whoever Allah grants success in believing in Him and obeying Him is the one who is granted success, and whoever He forsakes and does not grant success to is the one who is lost and ruined. Guidance and misguidance are from Allah alone.

We have created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind (Hell, in which Allah punishes whoever deserves punishment in the Hereafter). They have hearts with which they do not understand, so they hope for no reward and fear no punishment. They have eyes with which they do not look at the signs of Allah and His proofs, and they have ears with which they do not hear the verses of the Book of Allah so that they might reflect upon them. These are like cattle that do not comprehend what is said to them, nor understand what they see, nor use their hearts to distinguish good from evil and so tell them apart. Rather, they are further astray than cattle, for cattle perceive what benefits and harms them and follow their herdsman, whereas they are not like that. Those are the heedless, who are unmindful of faith in Allah and obedience to Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 180:

To Allah, glorified and exalted, belong the Most Beautiful Names (al-asma' al-husna), which indicate the perfection of His greatness, and all of His names are beautiful. So ask Him by His names for whatever you desire, and leave those who distort His names by adding to them, subtracting from them, or altering them, such as naming by them those who do not deserve them, as the polytheists named their idols with them, or giving them a meaning that neither Allah nor His Messenger intended. They will surely be recompensed for the evil deeds they used to do in this world, such as disbelief in Allah, deviating from the truth concerning His names, and denying His Messenger.

And among those whom We created is a virtuous community who guide themselves by the truth and call to it, and by it they judge and deal justly among people. They are the leaders of guidance from among those upon whom Allah has bestowed faith and righteous deeds.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 182:

As for those who denied Our signs and rejected them, and did not take heed from them, We shall gradually lead them on (istidraj) by opening to them the doors of provision and the means of livelihood in this world, so that they become deceived by what they have and think that they are upon something. Then We shall seize them suddenly, from where they do not know. This is a punishment from Allah for denying the proofs and signs of Allah.

I will grant respite to those who denied Our signs, until they think that they will not be punished, so that they increase in disbelief and transgression, and by this their punishment is doubled. Indeed, My plan is firm, meaning: strong and severe, which cannot be repelled by any power or by any stratagem.

Or did they not reflect, those who denied Our signs, so that they might contemplate with their minds and know that there is no madness in Muhammad (ﷺ)? He is only a warner to them of God's punishment for their disbelief in Him if they do not believe, a clear and sincere counsellor.

Have these deniers of God's signs not looked at the great dominion of God and His overpowering sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, and at everything God, exalted is His praise, has created in them? If they did, they would reflect on it and take a lesson from it, and they would consider their terms, which may have drawn near, so that they perish in their disbelief and arrive at God's punishment and His painful retribution. So by what warning and admonition, after the admonition of the Qur'an, will they believe and act?
Whomever Allah leaves astray from the path of guidance, there is no guide for him. And He leaves them in their disbelief, bewildering and wavering.

They ask you, O Messenger, the disbelievers of Makkah, about the Hour: when will it take place? Say to them: its knowledge is with Allah. None reveals it except Him. Its knowledge is heavy (ثَقُلَ عِلْمُهَا), hidden from the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. Neither an angel brought near nor a messenger prophet knows the time of its establishment. The Hour will not come except suddenly. These people ask you about it as though you were eager to know it, persistent in asking about it. Say to them: its knowledge is only with Allah, who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, but most people do not know that none knows it except Allah.

Say, O Messenger: "I have no power to bring about benefit for myself, nor to ward off harm that befalls me, except what God wills. Had I known the unseen, I would have taken the means by which I would know that they increase my welfare and gains, and I would have guarded against any evil before it occurred. I am only a messenger of God, sent to you, warning of His punishment and giving good news of His reward to a people who believe that I am a messenger of God and act according to His law."

He is the One who created you, O people, from a single soul, and created from it its mate, so that he might find comfort and tranquility in her. When he covered her, and the reference is to the kind of the two spouses among the descendants of Adam, she bore a light burden and carried it about, then sat and completed the pregnancy. When the time of her delivery drew near and she became heavy, the two spouses called upon their Lord: "If You give us a righteous, wholesome child, we will surely be among those who give thanks to You for the righteous child You have bestowed upon us."

When Allah granted the couple a righteous child, they ascribed partners to Allah concerning that child, whom Allah alone had created. They made him a servant of other than Allah. Exalted is Allah, and far above every form of association with Him.
Do these polytheists associate with Allah in worship His creatures, which are unable to create anything, rather they themselves are created?

The idols cannot help their worshippers, nor can they ward off harm even from themselves. If they create nothing, but are themselves created, and cannot repel harm from those who worship them or from themselves, then how can they be taken as gods alongside Allah? ﴿Indeed, this is the greatest injustice and the most foolish folly.﴾

If you, O polytheists, call these idols that you have worshipped besides Allah to guidance, they will not hear your call, nor will they follow you. It is the same whether you call upon them or remain silent about them, because they neither hear nor see, and they neither guide nor are guided.

This is a commentary on Surah al-A'raf (7), verse 194.

Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah, O polytheists, are servants owned by their Lord, just as you are owned by your Lord. So if you are truthful in your claim that they deserve any worship, then call upon them, and let them respond to you, if they are able to answer you and fulfil what you seek. And if they do not, it becomes clear that you are liars who have fabricated against Allah the gravest of falsehoods.

Is it that these deities and idols have feet with which they walk alongside you to fulfill your needs? Or do they have hands with which they repel harm from you and help you against whoever intends you evil and harm? Or do they have eyes with which they see, and then inform you of what they have witnessed and perceived of what is hidden from you, so that you do not see it? Or do they have ears with which they hear, and then tell you what you have not heard?

If your gods, which you worship, have none of these faculties, then what is the point of your worshipping them, when they are devoid of these things through which benefit may be brought or harm averted? Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists who worship idols: Call upon your gods whom you have made partners with God in worship, then unite in bringing evil and harm upon me, and do not delay me, but hasten it. For I am not concerned about your gods, because I rely on God's protection alone.

Surely my Protector is God, who takes charge of my protection and my victory. It is He who sent down the Qur'an with truth, and He takes charge of the righteous among His servants, granting them victory over their enemies and not abandoning them.
As for those whom you invoke, besides God, you polytheists, the deities, they cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.

If you call them to guidance, O polytheists, your deities will not hear your call. And you, O Messenger, see them facing you as though they were looking at you, yet they do not see, because they have no sight and no insight.

Accept what is easy from people's characters and deeds, O Prophet, you and your nation, and do not demand of them what is hard for them, lest they recoil. Enjoin every good word and beautiful deed, and turn away from disputing with the foolish and from matching the ignorant and dull-witted.

If Satan tempts you, O Prophet, with anger, or with a whisper that discourages you from good or urges you toward evil, then take refuge in Allah, seeking His protection. Indeed, He is All-Hearing of every utterance, All-Knowing of every deed.

Indeed, those who fear Allah among His creation, dreading His punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding what He has forbidden, when a passing whisper from Satan afflicts them, they remember what Allah has made obligatory upon them of obedience to Him and of repentance to Him. Then they are, at once, refraining from disobedience to Allah with insight, holding fast to the command of Allah, and disobeying Satan.

And the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked among misguided humans, are aided by the devils among the jinn in error and deviation. The devils among the jinn spare no effort in aiding the devils among humans in their error, and the devils among humans spare no effort in carrying out what the devils among the jinn inspire.

When you (O Messenger) do not bring these polytheists a sign that attests to your truthfulness, they say, "Why do you not invent it and fabricate it from yourself?" Say to them, O Messenger: "This is not mine to do, nor is it permissible for me to do it, for Allah only commanded me to follow what is revealed to me from Him, and it is this Qur'an that I recite to you as proofs and evidence from your Lord, and as a clarification that guides the believers to the straight path, and as a mercy by which Allah shows mercy to His believing servants."
And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it, O people, and remain silent, so that you may understand it, in the hope that Allah will show you mercy through it.

Remember, O Messenger, your Lord within yourself, with humility and lowliness before Allah, fearful and with a trembling heart before Him. Call upon Him in a voice between loud and quiet, at the beginning and the end of the day. And do not be among those who are heedless of the remembrance of Allah, and who are diverted from Him throughout the rest of their times.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 7, verse 206:

Indeed, those who are near your Lord, the angels, do not disdain to worship Allah. Rather, they submit to His commands, glorify Him by night and by day, and declare Him free of whatever is not fitting for Him. And to Him alone, with no partner, they prostrate.
